If you'd rather I write the code directly, just say so. First I'll read the current README opening, the Demo Scenario Launcher, and the proposal-alignment doc, so the prompt is grounded in facts that are already in the repo.

AGENTS.md has grown to 107KB because it tells everyone to add a README "update" section on every change, so moving the changelog out changes team process and the PR will flag it for Judy to approve. I'm writing the prompt next, including an AGENTS.md update for Bob.

The "First impression" Bob prompt is on your clipboard. In Bob, click **New Task** first (keep the earlier tasks separate so they're easier to export), choose **Agent** mode, paste with ⌘V, press Enter, and approve its actions.

**What the prompt has Bob do (two separate commits):**

**Commit 1: AI Planner page**
- Move the Demo Scenario Launcher **below the chat** and collapse it by default as "Demo tools (for presenters)". When a judge opens the page, the chat comes first.
- All the buttons keep working, and the demo script docs are updated to say "open Demo tools".

**Commit 2: README**
- Move the 49 changelog sections **unchanged** into `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, deleting none.
- Rewrite the README as a judge-facing overview, ideally under 15KB, covering:
  - the challenge track (Bring Your Own Challenge)
  - the problem statement
  - who it serves first (straight from your proposal: primary user, initial sponsor user, potential adopters, content partners, Penn as the first proposed pilot)
  - the solution
  - the Agentic AI archetypes, matched only to what's actually implemented
  - a technology statement (IBM Bob, watsonx Granite, Rust, React)
  - responsible AI, how to run it, the 3-minute demo, evaluation, current limits, and the team
- Fix the outdated "October 19–23".
- The video link is left as a "TODO (team)" placeholder. Bob is told not to invent anything: no made-up links or results.
- Update AGENTS.md so future changes are logged in `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, which keeps the README from bloating again.

The AGENTS.md change alters the team's workflow. When I open the PR, I'll flag it clearly for Judy to decide.

Once Bob commits, I'll check it: the planner page at desktop and phone width, that nothing was lost from the changelog, the README's length and accuracy (checked against the proposal and the code), and all the tests.Work in /Users/laitingting/ibm-campus_compass on the existing `Tingting` branch only. Do not create new branches and do not push. Read AGENTS.md first. First run `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (normal merge, never rebase) so you start from the latest main.

## Goal
Make the first impression clean for IBM judges. Two separate commits:
(A) the AI Planner page no longer opens with a developer panel;
(B) README.md becomes a short, judge-facing project overview, and the long development log moves to its own file.
Do not change any other feature.

## (A) Demo Scenario Launcher — commit 1
Today the AI Planner page (#planner) opens with the "Demo Scenario Launcher" panel (frontend/src/DemoLauncher.tsx, rendered in frontend/src/App.tsx around line 1052) ABOVE the chat. It says "No live AI" and pushes the chat down, so a judge's first view is a presenter tool.
- Move it BELOW the chat + draft-plan area and render it as a collapsed disclosure, closed by default: `<details>` with the summary "Demo tools (for presenters)". Remember open/closed for the session (sessionStorage, every read/write in try/catch).
- Keep every launcher button and behaviour exactly as it is (Prepare scenario, Recommend across interests, Simulate cancellation, Suggest replacement, Export final calendar, Restore previous demo) and keep the honest mode wording inside it.
- Update docs/demo-script.md so presenters know to open "Demo tools (for presenters)". Update tests/mode-labels.test.ts or any other test that relies on the old position.
- Check at 1280 px and 375 px: on opening #planner the first thing below the heading is the chat; the launcher is closed at the bottom and still works when opened.

## (B) README overview + CHANGELOG — commit 2
README.md is 107 KB, 915 lines and 49 "Update — …" sections, so the first screen is a PR #18 changelog. It also contains stale facts: "October 19–23, 2026" demo week (README.md ~line 784 and the "What works" section ~line 831), while the app and data/demo.json use Nov 2–6, 2026.

1. Move ALL development-log sections (every dated "## … — <date>" / "## Update — …" / "## PR #… review …" section, plus the older "Proposal-aligned MVP improvements", "Architecture update" etc.) into a new file docs/CHANGELOG.md, newest first, with a one-paragraph intro. Move them verbatim — do not rewrite history or delete entries.

2. Rewrite README.md as a concise overview (aim for under 15 KB) with these sections, in this order:
   - **Campus Compass** + one-sentence pitch.
   - **Challenge track:** Bring Your Own Challenge (higher education is not one of the four listed tracks).
   - **Problem statement:** universities already offer many academic, career and social opportunities, but they are fragmented across schools, departments and student organizations; students must discover, interpret and coordinate scattered information themselves (is it relevant, can students from another school attend, is RSVP needed, does it clash with classes, is there food), while organizers struggle to reach relevant students beyond their own channels. Present the institutional benefits (resource discoverability, cross-school reach) as hypotheses to validate, not results.
   - **Who it serves first:** primary user = university students exploring academic, career and social opportunities; initial sponsor user = a first-semester graduate student unfamiliar with campus information channels (especially international students); direct users = students; potential adopters = student-affairs and graduate-support offices; content partners = schools, departments, event organizers and student organizations providing approved event information. Penn is the first proposed pilot (where the team can reach users and verify sources), not the boundary of the product. Institutions adopting or paying is not assumed.
   - **Solution:** what the app does today, from the student's view (Home, Explore Events, AI Planner with visible filters, My Dashboard with Weekly Calendar and the full Day/Week/Month/Year calendar, Discussion Forum, Notifications, Settings), and the key rule that the student approves every addition and every add re-checks the latest schedule.
   - **Agentic AI approach:** map honestly to the lab's archetypes using what is implemented — Context-Aware Expert (plans around the student's interests, busy times, travel buffer and event updates), Cognitive Load Reducer (turns scattered listings into a short feasible week with plain "Why this fits" reasons), Human–AI Boundary Manager (clarifies ambiguous requests, never adds without approval, labels simulated vs watsonx answers). Do not claim anything that is not implemented.
   - **Technology statement:** IBM Bob (used to build features — say which ones only if recorded in bob_sessions/ or the changelog; link bob_sessions/), IBM watsonx.ai Granite (optional live interpreter plus ranking and model-written explanations via `PLANNER_PROVIDER=watsonx`; default is the deterministic simulated planner; every reply is labelled with the mode that produced it), Rust (Axum, Tokio, Serde) backend, React + TypeScript + Vite frontend, fictional data in data/.
   - **Responsible AI and data:** fictional events and profiles only, no personal information, browser-local state, student approval for every addition, deterministic validation after any model output, honest mode labels, data source register (link the existing "Data and assets register").
   - **Run it:** the existing "Run locally" commands, plus how to turn on watsonx (link docs/backend.md / wiki Using-watsonx). Demo week: Nov 2–6, 2026, America/New_York.
   - **Three-minute demo:** short walkthrough + link docs/demo-script.md. Add a line "Video: (YouTube link — to be added by the team)". Do NOT invent a link.
   - **Evaluation:** 2–3 sentences summarising docs/evaluation-report.md with a link; keep its honesty about live watsonx not being evaluated.
   - **Current limits:** accurate and current (fictional data, simulated by default, no real registrations or calendar sync, etc.).
   - **Team:** Judy (Jinru Zhou), Shuozhuo (Doris) Wang, Chenxi Liu, Tingting Lai, and the team branches table already in README.
   - **More:** links to docs/CHANGELOG.md, docs/, the GitHub Wiki, bob_sessions/.
   Use only facts that already exist in this repository (PRODUCT.md, docs/proposal-alignment.md, docs/demo-script.md, docs/backend.md, docs/evaluation-report.md, the existing README "Run locally / What works / Current boundaries / Data and assets register / Team branches" sections) or that are written in this prompt. If something is unknown, write "TODO (team)" rather than guessing.

3. Fix every stale "October 19–23" statement that describes the CURRENT app (keep historical changelog entries as they are).

4. AGENTS.md currently says "Before each push, update README.md with the completed changes…". Change it to: add a dated entry at the top of docs/CHANGELOG.md for each change, and keep README.md's overview accurate when a change affects it. (This is a team-process change; it will be flagged in the PR for Judy.)

5. Fix links that pointed to README headings that moved (e.g. `README.md#verification`, `README.md#…` in docs/, wiki/ and code comments) so they point to docs/CHANGELOG.md or the new README sections. Run `grep -rn "README.md#" --include=*.md --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.rs .` to find them.

## Verify before committing (report real numbers)
npm test, npm run build, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked, npm run test:api. Report README.md and docs/CHANGELOG.md sizes and confirm every changelog section that was in README is now in docs/CHANGELOG.md (same count of "## " headings moved). Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/#planner at 1280 px and 375 px and confirm the chat comes first.

## Commit
Two commits on `Tingting`: "AI Planner: move Demo Scenario Launcher into a collapsed presenter section" and "README: judge-facing overview; move development log to docs/CHANGELOG.md". State truthfully in the CHANGELOG entry that this work was done with IBM Bob. Do NOT push.

## Reply with
What changed in each commit, README/CHANGELOG sizes and heading counts, check results, any "TODO (team)" placeholders you left, commit hashes.

<role_definition>
You are Bob, a highly skilled software engineer with extensive knowledge in many programming languages, frameworks, design patterns, and best practices.
</role_definition>

<investigate_before_answering>
Never speculate about code you have not opened. If the user references a specific file, you MUST read the file before answering. Investigate and read relevant files before answering questions about the codebase. Never make any claims about code before investigating unless you are certain of the correct answer — give grounded and hallucination-free answers.
</investigate_before_answering>

<engineering_discipline>
Produce the minimal change that solves the problem. Do not add features, refactors, or abstractions beyond what was asked. Do not add error handling for scenarios that cannot happen. Do not clean up surrounding code that is unrelated to the task. If you write something and a simpler version would work, use the simpler version. Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
</engineering_discipline>

<tool_use>
- Choose the most appropriate tool for each step.
- Tools can be called in parallel when independent, but avoid running operations together that have dependencies (e.g., don't run edits and commands that depend on those edits in the same batch).
- If a tool fails, address the error before continuing.
- MCP server tools use IDs formatted as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Treat these as Model Context Protocol tools; the middle segment identifies the owning MCP server. Both segments may be truncated if the full name exceeds the 64-character API limit. Built-in and source tools use their normal IDs and are categorized by their descriptions and capability groups.
- Prefer native file tools (read_file, write_file, search_and_replace, insert_content, list_files) over shell commands for file operations — they need no additional user permissions. Use shell/execute tools only for operations that genuinely require them: builds, test runners, git commands, and system operations.

</tool_use>

<markdown_rules>
All responses should show any language construct or filename reference as a clickable link, exactly as [`filename OR language.declaration()`](relative/file/path.ext:line); line is required for syntax references and optional for filename links.
Mermaid diagrams (```mermaid code fences) are rendered natively in-chat.

</markdown_rules>

<auto_appended_context>
Each user message may contain an auto-appended <environment_details> section that includes potentially relevant information such as git status, active file, and relevant files modified externally since your last interaction. This section is automatically appended by the system to provide additional context that may possibly help you and is not part of the user's query.

Pay close attention to the <external_changes> sub-section — it lists files that were modified, deleted, or created outside of your actions. Before writing or editing any file, check whether it appears in <external_changes> and incorporate those changes to avoid conflicts.

</auto_appended_context>

<base_rules>
- Prefer editing tools (apply_diff, search_and_replace, insert_content) over write_file for existing files.
- When using write_file, provide the COMPLETE file content. Partial updates or placeholders are not acceptable.
- Be direct and technical. Do not start messages with "Great", "Certainly", "Okay", or "Sure".
- Follow existing code style and project conventions.
- Use available tools to accomplish tasks efficiently. Do not ask unnecessary follow-up questions.
- Do not stop when implementation looks complete. Finish the task only when all requested requirements are met and the resulting state is positive.
- Before reporting final completion, run the relevant validation for your changes. Use the checks that apply to the work you changed, such as lint, tests, typecheck, formatting, builds, or other project validation.
- Work is done when the changed work and any affected project state pass the required validation with no new warnings, failures, or unfinished requirements.

</base_rules>

<available_skills>
You have access to skills that provide specialized instructions for specific tasks. Review the available skills below. When a user's request matches a skill's description, activate it using the use_skill tool to load detailed instructions before proceeding. Only activate skills that are clearly relevant to the current task. Activate each skill once per current context window. If context was compacted and you need the instructions again, you may re-activate that skill. Only call use_skill for skills listed here — do not attempt to invoke skills not present in this list.
<skill>

  <description>Guide for building a custom MCP server from scratch — covers project scaffolding, the v2 registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt API, API key and OAuth authentication patterns, building and registering the server. Use when the user wants to create, build, or write a custom MCP server.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>configure-hooks</name>
  <description>Add, update, remove, or troubleshoot Bob lifecycle hooks. Use when the user wants to configure automatic commands or HTTPS requests for session, prompt, tool, or stop events.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>configure-mcp</name>
  <description>Add a new MCP server or diagnose an existing one — covers local vs remote transport, system dependency checks (node, docker, podman, python, uv), config schema validation, secrets handling, and scope. Use when the user wants to add, register, configure, or troubleshoot an MCP server.</description>
</skill>
<skill>
  <name>create-chart</name>
  <description>Full component schemas for the create_chart tool — covers all prop definitions for LineChart, BarChart, PieChart, ScatterChart, RadarChart, and BoxplotChart. Activate when building chart props.</description>
</skill>

</skill>

</skill>

Language Preference:
You should always speak and think in the "English" (en) language unless the user gives you instructions below to do otherwise.

Mode-specific Instructions:
You can write, modify, and refactor code in any programming language or framework. Always follow best practices and write clean, efficient, and maintainable code. Make sure to test your code thoroughly before submitting it. You can also provide code snippets, libraries, or frameworks to help the user accomplish their task. If you're following a set to do list as part of your task, use 'update_todo_list' as you progress — mark a task [-] in-progress only in the same update that marks the previous task [x] done, never as a standalone call before starting work.
</user_custom_instructions>

<project_rules>
The following rules are defined by this project and take precedence over your training defaults. They apply to every response for the duration of this session — do not revert to your defaults as the conversation grows longer. Before taking any action, check whether a project rule applies. Where rules from different sources conflict, the more specific source takes precedence: workspace rules override global rules, and mode-specific rules override common rules.

<rule>
  <filename>AGENTS.md</filename>
  <content># Campus Compass

A classroom campus-event planning demo for the IBM AI Experiential Learning Lab. Preserve fictional data, explicit student approval before calendar additions, and honest simulated-mode labels. Live watsonx is deferred; do not claim Bob development work unless the team actually performed and recorded it.

## Technology and structure

Use Rust for backend services and API endpoints, including future watsonx integration. Do not implement backend application code in Python. Use React and TypeScript for frontend source; JavaScript is the compiled browser runtime and may be used for tooling.

- `backend/src/`: Axum API, typed input validation, interpreter and deterministic scheduling.
- `frontend/src/`: React components, typed API client, browser-local state and labelled simulation fallback.
- `data/events.json`: shared fictional catalog. Rebuild both sides after edits.
- `dist/`: generated frontend output; edit source and run `npm run build`.

Read `docs/backend.md` when changing application architecture, API contracts, the interpreter, or local run/test setup. Keep the Rust and TypeScript fallback matching behavior aligned; the API integration test compares them. Revalidate against the latest schedule before adding an event or accepting asynchronous recommendations. Keep IBM secrets server-side.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# read_file — context focus
Always provide a `context_focus_query` string in your read_file calls. State the specific fact, value, or structure you need — not the general intent. For example, 'find the method signature of validate() and what exception it raises' is effective; 'read the file' or 'understand the code' is too vague and will cause important details to be lost. # office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).
**Backups:** edits apply directly to the user's file. Before the first edit of an existing file, the tool saves a backup and says so in its result — tell the user a backup was made.
- `operation:restore` — when the user wants the original back, or validation shows the file is corrupted.
- `operation:save_backup` — when the user is happy with the current state, so later restores return to it.
- `operation:delete_backup` — when the user is finished with the file. Ask before deleting.

Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.
Do NOT pass comma-separated patterns (e.g. "**/*.ts,**/*.tsx") — use a single pattern per call instead (e.g. "**/*.{ts,tsx}" or two separate calls).

Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.
Do NOT pass comma-separated patterns to `include` (e.g. "*.ts,*.tsx") — use a single pattern per call instead (e.g. "*.{ts,tsx}" or two separate calls).

# Three-minute Campus Compass demonstration

This is a repeatable fictional journey, not a real university or live IBM demonstration. Run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and `cargo run --locked`; use the Rust-served app. No credentials are needed. Go to AI Planner → Demo Scenario Launcher.

| Time | Presenter action | Say / show |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:25 | Prepare scenario → confirm. Expand Student context and limited availability. | “A fictional first-semester learning-sciences graduate student wants AI/research, career and social opportunities. Classes and a travel buffer limit availability. No career goal is required. Notes about major/goals stay local and are not interpreted.” |
| 0:25–0:50 | Recommend across interests. | Show three feasible topics rather than a single cluster. All selections use deterministic Rust rules; they are not watsonx responses. Explicit filters and access checks outrank diversity. |
| 0:50–1:20 | Read one card’s evidence and comparison. Open View details, then close it. | Show time/buffer fit, cost, location, RSVP, food distinctions and remaining uncertainty. “These are original fictional records; no external link or verified timestamp is invented. A comparison describes trade-offs, not a universally best choice.” |
| 1:20–1:50 | Add choices individually. For Designing your career story, complete the demo name/attendance confirmation. | No automatic additions or RSVPs. Cancel the form once if time permits, then approve. Show calendar changes. The current fixture suggests creative coding, a career workshop and an international tea table; if data/config changes, use the current displayed records. |
| 1:50–2:20 | Simulate cancellation → Suggest replacement. | Show the affected title and the two retained choices. The cancelled record is removed; the alternative remains a draft. Original constraints remain strict. If no match exists, explicitly choose which filter to change instead of quietly relaxing it. |
| 2:20–2:45 | Review replacement evidence and RSVP status; explicitly add/approve it. Export final calendar. | “The new selection is rechecked against the latest plan. The ICS export uses the configured demo week and time zone, and excludes cancellations. It does not connect an external account.” |
| 2:45–3:00 | Point to evaluation documentation; optionally show Restore previous demo. | “Twenty synthetic scenarios compare search, rules and context planning. Live watsonx: Not yet evaluated. Real student usefulness and organizer trust still need research.” |

Optional follow-up outside the three minutes: Settings → Team tools → Open synthetic-data review. Filter Unknown eligibility or Missing original URL. Missing external sources are expected for fictional records. The review is read-only; corrections go through a source-controlled team review and validation.

Preparing again resets only the guided state; the original browser-local state is archived once until Restore previous demo. Configuration changes create separate storage namespaces. Do not clear browser storage unless deliberately discarding that local archive.

After the main demonstration, show the update loop:

| Step | Action | Say / show |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Click the **bell** icon (topbar), **Check for updates** in Settings › Notifications, or the AI Planner's Event updates panel | "This applies the next pre-scripted batch of fictional catalog changes. Nothing is fetched from a server; everything is local." |
| 2 | Read the "What changed since your last check" feed | "Batch 1: a Career event was cancelled and a Social dinner is now full. Events in your plan are highlighted." |
| 3 | Click again for Batch 2 | "The AI lab time moved to an earlier slot — now it may conflict with another event. The room for Graduate makers night changed." |
| 4 | Click again for Batch 3 | Point to the "Needs confirmation" badge on the AI open studio card. "Two conflicting notices arrived for the same event — one says cancelled, one says the room changed. We do not choose which is correct; it shows 'Needs confirmation' until the student verifies directly." |
| 5 | Try to add or plan a cancelled/full event | "The backend rejects the attempt because the applied update IDs travel with every plan and validate request." |

Each event card shows its **Last checked** relative time from the catalog. Event detail panels show the full update notice and the "Needs confirmation" warning without picking either notice as authoritative.

## AI Planner: PR #18 review fixes — November 12, 2026

Small fixes from the PR #18 review, made with Claude Code (not IBM Bob):

- **Honest no-match wording.** When events match every filter but are already in the plan, conflict with it, or aren't open, the reply now says "The matching AI & education events on Tuesday in the morning are already in your plan, conflict with it, or aren't open." It no longer says "No AI & education events match that time window." The nearest alternatives are still offered. Same wording in Rust and the TypeScript fallback.
- **Excluded topics are visible.** A "not career" filter now shows as a `Not Career ×` chip. "Also at the same time" alternatives no longer include excluded topics.
- **"zero budget"** sets the free-admission filter again, as it did before this PR.

Verification: `npm test` 244/244 + 5/5 Wiki, `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test` 58/58, `cargo build`, `npm run test:api` all pass.

## AI Planner: free/availability rule, grammar, no-match wording, chip-removal lead — November 12, 2026 (round 3)

Four small fixes on top of round 2 (commit `4444022`).

### What was fixed (round 3)

1. **"free" vs availability rule (regression fix).** The round-2 rule (`\bfree\b` not before/after a person → free admission) was too broad: "ceramics free on Wednesday evening" no longer set `free: true`. The new rule: "free" means **availability** only when it follows a person pronoun or forms "free time/slot/period/hour/day" (e.g. "I'm free", "I'm only free Friday", "free slot on Thursday"). "free" next to or after an event or topic word means **free admission** ("free ceramics", "ceramics free", "free workshops"). "free food/meal/…" continues to set the food filter only. Updated in both `frontend/src/interpretation.ts` and `backend/src/interpreter.rs`. ## AI Planner: fresh search, visible filters, plain-language replies, and more synonyms — November 12, 2026 (round 1)

Four bugs in the AI Planner that a judge or new student would hit in the first few questions have been fixed.

### What was fixed

1. **Fresh search by default.** A new question ("any internship or job events?") now starts a clean search. Filters from the previous question only carry over when the message clearly builds on it — phrases like "only", "also", "instead", "what about", "but", "without" or a leading "and"/"or" count as follow-ups. Earlier, every question silently inherited all previous filters, so a "Wednesday evening" question would fail to find results if the previous question had asked for "free food".

2. **Active filter chips above the input box.** When the planner is filtering by topic, day, time, food or free admission, labelled chips now appear above the chat input: e.g. `Free food ×` `Wednesday ×` `Evening ×`. Clicking a chip removes that filter; "Clear all" removes all of them at once. Previously there was no way to see which filters were active without reading back through the chat history.

3. **No more dead ends — plain-language replies with alternatives.** When nothing matches, the planner no longer says "No synthetic catalog records satisfy these topic/day/time/cost/food filters. State which filter you want to change; none will be relaxed automatically." Instead it explains which filter produced no results and immediately offers the nearest alternatives, e.g. "Nothing on Wednesday evening has free food. Here are 4 options without that filter." The same logic runs in both Rust (`backend/src/planner.rs`) and TypeScript (`frontend/src/conversation.ts`).

4. **Everyday synonyms understood.** "internship" and "job" now map to Career; "practice English", "make friends", "meet people" and "language exchange" now map to Social. Both the Rust interpreter (`backend/src/interpreter.rs`) and the TypeScript fallback (`frontend/src/interpretation.ts`) were updated together. The "limited demo" guidance message also mentions these phrasings by example.

### Run and demo

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. In the AI Planner, try:

1. "is there anything with free food?" — three results, Free food chip appears
2. "I'm free Wednesday evening, what can I do?" — now shows 4 Wednesday-evening results (Fresh search; no longer inherits the free-food filter)
3. "any internship or job events?" — now shows career events (new synonym; no longer filtered to Wednesday)
4. "something to help me find an internship" — understood as Career

### Verification

`npm test` (185 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `node --import tsx --test tests/*.test.ts` (185 tests), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` (41 tests), `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit` + Vite), and `npm run test:api` all pass. The integration test's diagnostic assertion was updated from `/scheduling conflicts/` to `/Nothing matches that time window/` to match the new plain-language reply. Checked in the browser at 1280px and 375px: filter chips appear and dismiss correctly, Wednesday-evening questions return results without a prior free-food filter, career queries return multiple events, and "start over" clears all chips. Only simulated mode was tested; watsonx mode uses the same carry-over and synonym logic and should benefit from the same changes.

### Limitations

- The follow-up detection is heuristic (keyword-based). A message like "but make it on Tuesday" carries over previous filters as intended, but an unusual phrasing without a follow-up keyword starts fresh. Watsonx mode sends the full `previous` constraints to the model, so the model can decide; this fix only changes the browser's default.
- Filter chips show the constraints stored in `state.constraints`, which are updated after each successful query. They do not reflect mid-clarification constraints (pending clarification state).

## Back and swipe-back between tabs — November 10, 2026

Back (and the swipe-back gesture) no longer steps through tabs you visited before. Sidebar tabs (Dashboard, My Calendar, Explore Events, Discussion Forum, AI Planner, Saved Events, Profile, Settings) are on the same level, so on any of them Back is blocked and you stay where you are. Back only closes sub-pages, innermost first:

| Sub-page | Back returns to |
| --- | --- |
| Event details (from any page) | The page underneath |
| A community in the forum (also from an event's "Related communities" link or a `#forum?community=…` URL) | All forum posts |
| A forum post or the Create post editor | The post list (or the open community) |
| Synthetic-data review (Settings → Team tools) | Settings |

How it works (`frontend/src/navigation.ts`): switching tabs replaces the browser history entry instead of adding one. Back closes the innermost open sub-page; on a tab, nothing happens. Forward is ignored. The logo link no longer adds a history entry on each click.

**Why the first version still let a real swipe leave the site (fixed November 11):** Chrome and Safari skip history entries that a page adds without a user gesture, so a site can't trap visitors. The app used to add its guard entry on page load and re-add it inside the Back handler. Neither counts as a gesture, so a real swipe or Back press went straight past the guard and left the website. Scripted `history.back()` doesn't apply that skipping, which is why the earlier checks passed. Now the app adds entries only while you're tapping, clicking or typing: each interaction tops up a cushion of 3 Back presses, and each Back uses one.

Verification:
- `npm test` (91 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build` and `npm run test:api` pass.
- In a fresh browser tab with another page in its history before the app, I used real clicks and recorded every history entry the app added: all of them were added during a user gesture.
- After clicking Explore Events, three Backs in a row stayed on Explore Events.
- Event details: Back closed them, then the next Backs were absorbed.
- Forum: community → post, then Back, Back, Back closed the post, then the community, then was absorbed.
- Forward changed nothing.

Limitations:
- **No protection before the first interaction.** A Back or swipe before you tap, click or type anything leaves the site, because browsers ignore entries added without a gesture.
- **At most 3 Backs absorbed.** A fourth Back in a row without touching the page leaves.
- **Not tried with a real swipe.** I checked with real clicks plus `history.back()` in Chromium; a real swipe on a Mac trackpad, iPhone or Android device wasn't tried.

## Architecture update — October 18, 2026

Enrollment, planning conversations and request interpretation now own their rules in separate modules. This keeps the calendar beside chat and mandatory demo RSVP flow while making asynchronous behavior testable through the same interfaces the UI uses.

| Change | What teammates should expect |
| --- | --- |
| Enrollment ownership | One module owns RSVP gating, pending additions, current-schedule checks and calendar/RSVP updates. Reset discards obsolete confirmations and errors; removing an event clears its RSVP. |
| Conversation ownership | Chat and replacement share request validity and busy-state handling. New chat/reset discard old results; changed schedules reject outdated suggestions. Replacement preserves every filter until the student explicitly changes it. |
| Consistent interpretation | “Professional”, “ceramics”, “balance”, “snack” and “refreshment” reach the interpreter. Rust and browser simulation distinguish unsupported requests from understood requests with no matches, and reject invalid clock input such as “before 11:99 am”. |
| Calendar beside chat | The **My calendar** button at the top right of AI Planner toggles a calendar panel on the right without leaving the conversation. It replaces the draft sidebar while open. On narrow screens it stacks below chat. |
| Actions in AI responses | New recommendation messages contain event cards with **View details** and **Add to calendar** buttons. Added events show a disabled confirmation button. Unavailable events show the reason. |
| Mandatory RSVP | Adding an event marked **RSVP required** opens a registration dialog. A demo attendee name and an explicit attendance checkbox are required before **Complete RSVP & add** can succeed. Cancelling or pressing Escape leaves the calendar unchanged. |
| Automatic calendar updates | A successful addition immediately updates the planner panel, dashboard and main calendar. Drop-in events can be added directly. Removing an event also clears its demo RSVP confirmation. |
| Shared enrollment validation | Every Add entry point—chat, draft plan, dashboard, Explore Events and event details—uses the same flow. Rust and the offline TypeScript fallback both enforce RSVP and current availability. |

The registration dialog is a **demo RSVP page** inside the app. It does not contact an organizer, reserve a real seat, charge a fee, or send a confirmation email. Use a fictional display name. There is no external registration website or live calendar integration.

## AI Planner: free/availability rule, grammar, no-match wording, chip-removal lead — November 12, 2026 (round 3)

Four small fixes on top of round 2 (commit `4444022`).

### What was fixed (round 3)

1. **"free" vs availability rule (regression fix).** The round-2 rule (`\bfree\b` not before/after a person → free admission) was too broad: "ceramics free on Wednesday evening" no longer set `free: true`. The new rule: "free" means **availability** only when it follows a person pronoun or forms "free time/slot/period/hour/day" (e.g. "I'm free", "I'm only free Friday", "free slot on Thursday"). "free" next to or after an event or topic word means **free admission** ("free ceramics", "ceramics free", "free workshops"). "free food/meal/…" continues to set the food filter only. Updated in both `frontend/src/interpretation.ts` and `backend/src/interpreter.rs`. The frozen evaluation scenario H04 ("ceramics free on Wednesday evening") is confirmed restored: it no longer returns the $12 ceramics workshop.

2. **Grammar — "3 options that **fit** together".** Plurals now correctly say "fit"; singular is still "1 option that **fits** together". Same for "1 alternative" vs "2 alternatives". Updated in `frontend/src/conversation.ts`.

3. **No-match wording — topic included, "Here are N" not "Here N".** The no-match messages now name the topic and use correct verb agreement, e.g. "No AI & education events on Monday match that time window. Here are 4 options at other times." The helper function is `buildNoMatchAlts` (TypeScript) and `no_match_reason` (Rust); both updated in lock-step. A "free admission" relaxation step was added as step 2 (after food).

4. **Chip-removal reply starts with "Removed [label]."** When a chip is removed, the planner result message now starts with "Removed Thursday. I found 3 options…" instead of "I found 3 options…". Implemented by passing a `replyPrefix` to `run()` in `conversation.ts`. The separate "Here's what fits now:" prefix message was removed to avoid two consecutive assistant messages.

### New tests (round 3)

`tests/planner-round2.test.ts` adds 17 more TypeScript tests (total 47 new since round 1): free vs availability tests ("ceramics free", "free ceramics", "I'm free", "I'm only free on Friday", "free food", "free slot"), grammar tests, no-match topic inclusion, and chip-removal lead. `backend/src/interpreter.rs` adds 3 more Rust tests (total 15 new): `free_ceramics_sets_free_admission`, `ceramics_free_on_wednesday_sets_free_admission`, `im_only_free_on_friday_no_admission`.

## AI Planner: chip removal re-runs search, free-admission wording, alternatives, fuzzy phrases, overlap cards — November 12, 2026 (round 2)

Six issues found in hands-on testing of commit `1ede074` have been addressed in this second round.

### What was fixed (round 2)

1. **Clicking a filter chip × re-runs the search.** Previously the chip disappeared but the suggestion cards did not change. Now `conversation.removeFilter()` posts a short confirmation line ("Removed Wednesday filter. Here's what fits now:") and immediately re-runs the planner with the remaining constraints. "Clear all" posts "Filters cleared. Tell me what you're looking for." The chip-building logic is extracted into `frontend/src/filterChips.ts` (`filterChips()` / `removeChip()`) for unit testing.

2. **"free" no longer means free admission.** "I'm free Wednesday evening" and "anything with free food?" no longer add a "Free admission" chip. Free admission is now set only for explicit phrases: "free admission", "free entry", "free to attend", "free of charge", "no cost", "costs nothing", "without paying", "zero cost". Both `frontend/src/interpretation.ts` and `backend/src/interpreter.rs` were updated in lock-step. "Free meal/lunch/dinner/snacks/coffee/pizza" sets the food filter only.

3. **No-match duplication fixed; alternative events shown as cards.** The no-match text was appearing twice (once from the Rust diagnostic in `plan.notice`, once from the TypeScript fallback). The fix: when the Rust planner returns a no-match diagnostic, use it as the response text and build the local alternative list (IDs only) for the suggestion cards. The no-match function (`buildNoMatchAlts`) now returns both `{ text, ids }` so the cards are populated. The browser-fallback path shows the unavailability notice followed by the plain-language no-match text.

4. **Fuzzy phrase matching.** "practice **my** English", "make **some/new** friends", "meet **new** people", "find **an** internship", "get **a** job" now work. Both interpreters use flexible regexes that allow one or two small words between key terms. The "limited demo" reply now shows 3 clickable example-request buttons (rendered as `<button>` elements that send that text into the chat). A new `examples` field on `Message` carries these; a new `LimitedDemoHint` error class in `api.ts` carries them to `conversation.ts`.

5. **Overlap alternatives shown as "Also at the same time" cards.** When the planner finds 1 conflict-free pick but there are other eligible events at the same time (e.g. Wednesday evening: 3 eligible, 1 conflict-free), the message says "I found 1 option that fits together, plus 2 alternatives at the same time" and shows them below a labelled "Also at the same time:" section. They are clearly separate from the main pick. A new `overlapIds` field on `Message` carries them.

6. **New tests.** `tests/planner-round2.test.ts` adds 30 TypeScript tests covering all five items above: free-admission wording, phrase synonyms, `filterChips` labels, fresh-search carry-over, no-match plain-language fallback (browser mode), and overlap detection. `backend/src/interpreter.rs` adds 12 Rust tests covering the same free-admission and synonym rules, the no-match diagnostic wording, and fresh-parse carry-over.

## AI Planner: fresh search, visible filters, plain-language replies, and more synonyms — November 12, 2026 (round 1)

Four bugs in the AI Planner that a judge or new student would hit in the first few questions have been fixed.

### What was fixed

1. **Fresh search by default.** A new question ("any internship or job events?") now starts a clean search. Filters from the previous question only carry over when the message clearly builds on it — phrases like "only", "also", "instead", "what about", "but", "without" or a leading "and"/"or" count as follow-ups. Earlier, every question silently inherited all previous filters, so a "Wednesday evening" question would fail to find results if the previous question had asked for "free food".

2. **Active filter chips above the input box.** When the planner is filtering by topic, day, time, food or free admission, labelled chips now appear above the chat input: e.g. `Free food ×` `Wednesday ×` `Evening ×`. Clicking a chip removes that filter; "Clear all" removes all of them at once. Previously there was no way to see which filters were active without reading back through the chat history.

3. **No more dead ends — plain-language replies with alternatives.** When nothing matches, the planner no longer says "No synthetic catalog records satisfy these topic/day/time/cost/food filters. State which filter you want to change; none will be relaxed automatically." Instead it explains which filter produced no results and immediately offers the nearest alternatives, e.g. "Nothing on Wednesday evening has free food. Here are 4 options without that filter." The same logic runs in both Rust (`backend/src/planner.rs`) and TypeScript (`frontend/src/conversation.ts`).

4. **Everyday synonyms understood.** "internship" and "job" now map to Career; "practice English", "make friends", "meet people" and "language exchange" now map to Social. Both the Rust interpreter (`backend/src/interpreter.rs`) and the TypeScript fallback (`frontend/src/interpretation.ts`) were updated together. The "limited demo" guidance message also mentions these phrasings by example.

### Run and demo

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. In the AI Planner, try:

1. "is there anything with free food?" — three results, Free food chip appears
2. "I'm free Wednesday evening, what can I do?" — now shows 4 Wednesday-evening results (Fresh search; no longer inherits the free-food filter)
3. "any internship or job events?" — now shows career events (new synonym; no longer filtered to Wednesday)
4. "something to help me find an internship" — understood as Career

### Verification

`npm test` (185 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `node --import tsx --test tests/*.test.ts` (185 tests), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` (41 tests), `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit` + Vite), and `npm run test:api` all pass. The integration test's diagnostic assertion was updated from `/scheduling conflicts/` to `/Nothing matches that time window/` to match the new plain-language reply. Checked in the browser at 1280px and 375px: filter chips appear and dismiss correctly, Wednesday-evening questions return results without a prior free-food filter, career queries return multiple events, and "start over" clears all chips. Only simulated mode was tested; watsonx mode uses the same carry-over and synonym logic and should benefit from the same changes.

### Limitations

- The follow-up detection is heuristic (keyword-based). A message like "but make it on Tuesday" carries over previous filters as intended, but an unusual phrasing without a follow-up keyword starts fresh. Watsonx mode sends the full `previous` constraints to the model, so the model can decide; this fix only changes the browser's default.
- Filter chips show the constraints stored in `state.constraints`, which are updated after each successful query. They do not reflect mid-clarification constraints (pending clarification state).

## Back and swipe-back between tabs — November 10, 2026

Back (and the swipe-back gesture) no longer steps through tabs you visited before. Sidebar tabs (Dashboard, My Calendar, Explore Events, Discussion Forum, AI Planner, Saved Events, Profile, Settings) are on the same level, so on any of them Back is blocked and you stay where you are. Back only closes sub-pages, innermost first:

| Sub-page | Back returns to |
| --- | --- |
| Event details (from any page) | The page underneath |
| A community in the forum (also from an event's "Related communities" link or a `#forum?community=…` URL) | All forum posts |
| A forum post or the Create post editor | The post list (or the open community) |
| Synthetic-data review (Settings → Team tools) | Settings |

How it works (`frontend/src/navigation.ts`): switching tabs replaces the browser history entry instead of adding one. Back closes the innermost open sub-page; on a tab, nothing happens. Forward is ignored. The logo link no longer adds a history entry on each click.

**Why the first version still let a real swipe leave the site (fixed November 11):** Chrome and Safari skip history entries that a page adds without a user gesture, so a site can't trap visitors. The app used to add its guard entry on page load and re-add it inside the Back handler. Neither counts as a gesture, so a real swipe or Back press went straight past the guard and left the website. Scripted `history.back()` doesn't apply that skipping, which is why the earlier checks passed. Now the app adds entries only while you're tapping, clicking or typing: each interaction tops up a cushion of 3 Back presses, and each Back uses one.

Verification:
- `npm test` (91 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build` and `npm run test:api` pass.
- In a fresh browser tab with another page in its history before the app, I used real clicks and recorded every history entry the app added: all of them were added during a user gesture.
- After clicking Explore Events, three Backs in a row stayed on Explore Events.
- Event details: Back closed them, then the next Backs were absorbed.
- Forum: community → post, then Back, Back, Back closed the post, then the community, then was absorbed.
- Forward changed nothing.

Limitations:
- **No protection before the first interaction.** A Back or swipe before you tap, click or type anything leaves the site, because browsers ignore entries added without a gesture.
- **At most 3 Backs absorbed.** A fourth Back in a row without touching the page leaves.
- **Not tried with a real swipe.** I checked with real clicks plus `history.back()` in Chromium; a real swipe on a Mac trackpad, iPhone or Android device wasn't tried.

## Update — November 4, 2026: optional IBM watsonx interpreter

The AI Planner can now use IBM watsonx.ai (Granite, Dallas `us-south`) to understand chat messages. It is **off by default**: without configuration the app runs the simulated planner exactly as before, and no credentials are needed.

| Change | What teammates should expect |
| --- | --- |
| Live interpreter option | Starting Rust with `PLANNER_PROVIDER=watsonx` makes `/api/plan` send the student's message and the previous filters to watsonx.ai. The model returns only search filters (topics, days, times, food, cost, number of options). The schedule, profile, names and chat history are not sent. |
| Trusted matching unchanged | Model output must be a JSON object with only known fields and must pass `Constraints::validate`. Rust's deterministic planner still picks every event, so the model cannot invent event IDs, eligibility or food. Adding an event still needs the student's click and a fresh validation. |
| Honest labels | The chat status shows **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** only when watsonx actually answered. If watsonx times out (6 s), rejects authentication, errors or returns invalid output, that request uses the simulated planner, the label reads **Rust planner · Simulated**, and the reply starts with "IBM watsonx was unavailable…". The offline browser fallback is unchanged. |
| Secrets stay on the server | The API key is read from the server environment, is exchanged for an IBM IAM token server-side, and never appears in API responses, logs or browser code. `.env` files are git-ignored. |
| Health endpoint | `GET /api/health` now also reports `watsonx_configured`. `watsonx_connected` is true only after the most recent live call succeeded. |

### Run with watsonx

```sh
cp .env.example .env    # then fill in WATSONX_API_KEY and WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
set -a; source .env; set +a
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

The startup line says which planner is active. `WATSONX_URL` defaults to `https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com` and `WATSONX_MODEL_ID` to `ibm/granite-4-h-small`, the Granite chat model offered in the lab's watsonx Challenge Sandbox. If your project lists a different Granite chat model, set its ID instead. Leave `PLANNER_PROVIDER` unset (or `simulated`) for the credential-free classroom demo. Details: [docs/backend.md](docs/backend.md#ibm-watsonx-interpreter).

- `backend/src/watsonx.rs`: `WatsonxInterpreter` (IAM token caching, `POST /ml/v1/text/chat`, JSON-only parsing, validation, timeout) and its mock-server tests.

arguments.content:
# Campus Compass

A conversational campus-event planner that helps university students discover and coordinate academic, career and social opportunities during their first semester — built as a demonstration for the IBM AI Experiential Learning Lab.

## Challenge track

**Bring Your Own Challenge.** Higher education is not one of the four listed tracks; this project names it as its own challenge statement.

## Problem statement

Universities already offer many academic, career and social opportunities, but they are fragmented across schools, departments and student organizations. Students must discover, interpret and coordinate scattered information themselves: Is this event relevant to me? Can students from another school attend? Is RSVP needed? Does it clash with my classes? Is there food? Organizers struggle to reach relevant students beyond their own channels.

The institutional benefits — improved resource discoverability, cross-school reach, reduced scheduling friction — are hypotheses to validate, not results. No student interviews or organizer research have been conducted yet.

## Who it serves first

| Role | Description |
|---|---|
| **Primary user** | University students exploring academic, career and social opportunities |
| **Initial sponsor user** | A first-semester graduate student unfamiliar with campus information channels (especially international students) |
| **Direct users** | Students browsing, planning and RSVPing |
| **Potential adopters** | Student-affairs and graduate-support offices |
| **Content partners** | Schools, departments, event organizers and student organizations providing approved event information |

**Proposed first pilot:** the University of Pennsylvania, where the team can reach users and verify sources. This is not the boundary of the product; institutions adopting or paying is not assumed.

## Solution

What the app does today, from the student's view:

- **Home** — announcement carousel, browse-by-category tiles (Academic, Career, Social, Workshops, Wellbeing, Arts, Free food), and a preference-ranked list of upcoming events.
- **Explore Events** — searchable, filterable event cards with access conditions, food, RSVP status and source provenance.
- **AI Planner** — conversational chat with visible filter chips; a draft-plan sidebar; and a "What I'm working with" panel showing interests, busy times, travel buffer and planned events. The student approves every addition; every add re-checks the latest schedule. Optional watsonx mode (see below).
- **My Dashboard** — Weekly Calendar strip with week navigation; **Full Calendar** sub-page with Day/Week/Month/Year views.
- **Discussion Forum** — searchable communities, local posts, join/leave, related events.
- **Notifications** — bell dropdown, unread badge, filterable Notifications page, per-notification messages.
- **Settings** — time zone, 15-minute travel buffer, AI connection mode, demo reset, synthetic-data review (Team tools).

## Agentic AI approach

The planner is mapped to three of the lab's archetypes based on what is actually implemented:

| Archetype | How it shows up |
|---|---|
| **Context-Aware Expert** | Plans around the student's stated interests, existing busy times, travel buffer and live event updates. Access conditions, conflicts and cancellations are re-checked on every add. |
| **Cognitive Load Reducer** | Turns scattered event listings into a short feasible week plan with plain "Why this fits" reasons for each pick (interest match, schedule fit, cost, RSVP status). |
| **Human–AI Boundary Manager** | Clarifies ambiguous requests (AM/PM, excluded days, unsupported budgets) before suggesting anything. Never adds an event without the student's explicit approval. Labels every reply with the mode that produced it (Simulated or IBM watsonx). |

## Technology

- **IBM Bob** — used to build features in this project; see [`bob_sessions/`](bob_sessions/) for exported task histories. (The Calendar Day/Week/Month/Year views, the AI Planner improvements, and this README rewrite were done with IBM Bob; earlier work was done with Claude Code or Codex as noted in [`docs/CHANGELOG.md`](docs/CHANGELOG.md).)
- **IBM watsonx.ai Granite** — optional live interpreter and ranker via `PLANNER_PROVIDER=watsonx`. Default is the deterministic simulated planner. Every reply is labelled with the mode that produced it.
- **Rust** (Axum, Tokio, Serde) — backend API, typed validation, deterministic scheduling logic.
- **React + TypeScript + Vite** — frontend; browser-local state; explicitly labelled simulation fallback when the backend is unavailable.
- **Fictional data** in [`data/`](data/) — 48 original fictional events; no real university records.

## Responsible AI and data

- Fictional events and profiles only; no personal information is collected or stored server-side.
- All state is browser-local; nothing is shared between users.
- Student approval required for every calendar addition.
- Deterministic validation runs after any model output; the model cannot invent event IDs or eligibility.
- Every reply is labelled with the mode that produced it (Simulated · No live AI, or IBM watsonx · Granite).
- See [Data and assets register](#data-and-assets-register) below.

## Run it

Install Rust stable and Node.js 22.12+. From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. The chat status label under AI Planner shows which planner answered: **Rust planner · Simulated** (default, no credentials needed), **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** (live Granite), or **Browser fallback · Simulated** (the server is not running).

For frontend development, run `npm run dev` alongside Rust.

**Demo week:** Nov 2–6, 2026, America/New_York time.

**To enable watsonx:**

```sh
cp .env.example .env    # fill in WATSONX_API_KEY and WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
set -a; source .env; set +a
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

See [docs/backend.md](docs/backend.md) for full backend and watsonx setup, and the [Wiki — Using watsonx](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Using-watsonx) for step-by-step instructions.

## Three-minute demo

Follow [docs/demo-script.md](docs/demo-script.md). Open AI Planner and expand **Demo tools (for presenters)** at the bottom of the page to reach the Demo Scenario Launcher.

**Video:** TODO (team — add YouTube link before submission)

## Evaluation

[docs/evaluation-report.md](docs/evaluation-report.md) reports 20 frozen synthetic scenarios (12 development, 8 held-out) comparing keyword/category search, deterministic rules and the Rust context planner. The Rust planner has zero measured conflict or eligibility violations on this suite and achieves 100% diversity on development scenarios. **Live watsonx: Not yet evaluated.** This is a small visible synthetic benchmark, not proof of live AI value or user benefit.

## Current limits

- **Fictional data only.** No real university events, registrations or calendar sync.
- **Simulated by default.** The deterministic planner requires no credentials. Live watsonx is optional and has not been evaluated against real queries.
- **No real RSVPs.** The demo RSVP dialog is fictional; no organizer receives it.
- **No external calendar sync.** `.ics` export only.
- **Browser-local state.** Nothing is shared between browsers or users.
- **Penn pilot is proposed, not started.** No user interviews or organizer research have been conducted.
- **Mascot asset provenance.** The cat image was supplied for this website. Its third-party license has not been independently verified; confirm before any broader public distribution.

## Team

Judy (Jinru Zhou), Shuozhuo (Doris) Wang, Chenxi Liu, Tingting Lai.

### Team branches

The shared starting branch is `main`. Individual work branches are `Judy`, `Doris`, `Bella`, and `Tingting` (case-sensitive). Start work on your own branch and open a pull request into `main` for team review.

```sh
git clone git@github.com:judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass.git
cd ibm-campus_compass
git switch Judy
```

Replace `Judy` with your assigned branch name.

## More

- [docs/CHANGELOG.md](docs/CHANGELOG.md) — full development log (40 entries moved from this README)
- [docs/](docs/) — backend guide, evaluation methodology, demo script, proposal alignment, wiki publishing
- [GitHub Wiki](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki) — teammate step-by-step guides (Getting started, Using watsonx, IBM Bob, Team workflow)
- [bob_sessions/](bob_sessions/) — exported IBM Bob task histories (required for judging)

---

## Data and assets register

All 48 event records were originally authored for this prototype. No campus websites, personal calendars, social media, confidential records or real student data were ingested. Event locations, communities, and discussion participants are fictional. Dates use a fixed demonstration week (Nov 2–6, 2026).

The cat image was supplied by the user for this website and is used unchanged. Its original third-party authorship/license has not been independently verified. Before public distribution beyond the team's intended demo, the team should record the original asset provenance/permission. No external images or fonts are loaded. Compass and interface icons are original SVG geometry; poster panels are original HTML/CSS typographic artwork.

Names in the team credit were supplied or inferred from the user's account context. Demo profile fields are editable and are stored only in the viewer's browser.

## Verification

Run these from the repository root before sharing application changes:

```sh
npm test
npm run build
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked
cargo build --locked
npm run test:api
```

The API integration suite starts a temporary local Rust server; allow localhost listeners in your environment. Build the Rust binary and frontend before running it.

## GitHub Wiki

Wiki page sources live in [`wiki/`](wiki/). After changes merge into `main`, the Publish GitHub Wiki workflow updates the [project Wiki](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki). One-time credential setup and publishing details are in [`docs/github-wiki.md`](docs/github-wiki.md).

The new rule: "free" means **availability** only when it follows a person pronoun or forms "free time/slot/period/hour/day" (e.g. "I'm free", "I'm only free Friday", "free slot on Thursday"). "free" next to or after an event or topic word means **free admission** ("free ceramics", "ceramics free", "free workshops"). "free food/meal/…" continues to set the food filter only. Updated in both `frontend/src/interpretation.ts` and `backend/src/interpreter.rs`. The frozen evaluation scenario H04 ("ceramics free on Wednesday evening") is confirmed restored: it no longer returns the $12 ceramics workshop.

2. **Grammar — "3 options that **fit** together".** Plurals now correctly say "fit"; singular is still "1 option that **fits** together". Same for "1 alternative" vs "2 alternatives". Updated in `frontend/src/conversation.ts`.

3. **No-match wording — topic included, "Here are N" not "Here N".** The no-match messages now name the topic and use correct verb agreement, e.g. "No AI & education events on Monday match that time window. Here are 4 options at other times." The helper function is `buildNoMatchAlts` (TypeScript) and `no_match_reason` (Rust); both updated in lock-step. A "free admission" relaxation step was added as step 2 (after food).

4. **Chip-removal reply starts with "Removed [label]."** When a chip is removed, the planner result message now starts with "Removed Thursday. I found 3 options…" instead of "I found 3 options…". ## AI Planner: fresh search, visible filters, plain-language replies, and more synonyms — November 12, 2026 (round 1)

Four bugs in the AI Planner that a judge or new student would hit in the first few questions have been fixed.

### What was fixed

1. **Fresh search by default.** A new question ("any internship or job events?") now starts a clean search. Filters from the previous question only carry over when the message clearly builds on it — phrases like "only", "also", "instead", "what about", "but", "without" or a leading "and"/"or" count as follow-ups. Earlier, every question silently inherited all previous filters, so a "Wednesday evening" question would fail to find results if the previous question had asked for "free food".

2. **Active filter chips above the input box.** When the planner is filtering by topic, day, time, food or free admission, labelled chips now appear above the chat input: e.g. `Free food ×` `Wednesday ×` `Evening ×`. Clicking a chip removes that filter; "Clear all" removes all of them at once. Previously there was no way to see which filters were active without reading back through the chat history.

3. **No more dead ends — plain-language replies with alternatives.** When nothing matches, the planner no longer says "No synthetic catalog records satisfy these topic/day/time/cost/food filters. State which filter you want to change; none will be relaxed automatically." Instead it explains which filter produced no results and immediately offers the nearest alternatives, e.g. "Nothing on Wednesday evening has free food. Here are 4 options without that filter." The same logic runs in both Rust (`backend/src/planner.rs`) and TypeScript (`frontend/src/conversation.ts`).

4. **Everyday synonyms understood.** "internship" and "job" now map to Career; "practice English", "make friends", "meet people" and "language exchange" now map to Social. Both the Rust interpreter (`backend/src/interpreter.rs`) and the TypeScript fallback (`frontend/src/interpretation.ts`) were updated together. The "limited demo" guidance message also mentions these phrasings by example.

### Run and demo

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. In the AI Planner, try:

1. "is there anything with free food?" — three results, Free food chip appears
2. "I'm free Wednesday evening, what can I do?" — now shows 4 Wednesday-evening results (Fresh search; no longer inherits the free-food filter)
3. "any internship or job events?" — now shows career events (new synonym; no longer filtered to Wednesday)
4. "something to help me find an internship" — understood as Career

### Verification

`npm test` (185 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `node --import tsx --test tests/*.test.ts` (185 tests), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` (41 tests), `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit` + Vite), and `npm run test:api` all pass. The integration test's diagnostic assertion was updated from `/scheduling conflicts/` to `/Nothing matches that time window/` to match the new plain-language reply. Checked in the browser at 1280px and 375px: filter chips appear and dismiss correctly, Wednesday-evening questions return results without a prior free-food filter, career queries return multiple events, and "start over" clears all chips. Only simulated mode was tested; watsonx mode uses the same carry-over and synonym logic and should benefit from the same changes.

### Limitations

- The follow-up detection is heuristic (keyword-based). A message like "but make it on Tuesday" carries over previous filters as intended, but an unusual phrasing without a follow-up keyword starts fresh. Watsonx mode sends the full `previous` constraints to the model, so the model can decide; this fix only changes the browser's default.
- Filter chips show the constraints stored in `state.constraints`, which are updated after each successful query. They do not reflect mid-clarification constraints (pending clarification state).

## Back and swipe-back between tabs — November 10, 2026

Back (and the swipe-back gesture) no longer steps through tabs you visited before. Sidebar tabs (Dashboard, My Calendar, Explore Events, Discussion Forum, AI Planner, Saved Events, Profile, Settings) are on the same level, so on any of them Back is blocked and you stay where you are. Back only closes sub-pages, innermost first:

| Sub-page | Back returns to |
| --- | --- |
| Event details (from any page) | The page underneath |
| A community in the forum (also from an event's "Related communities" link or a `#forum?community=…` URL) | All forum posts |
| A forum post or the Create post editor | The post list (or the open community) |
| Synthetic-data review (Settings → Team tools) | Settings |

How it works (`frontend/src/navigation.ts`): switching tabs replaces the browser history entry instead of adding one. Back closes the innermost open sub-page; on a tab, nothing happens. Forward is ignored. The logo link no longer adds a history entry on each click.

**Why the first version still let a real swipe leave the site (fixed November 11):** Chrome and Safari skip history entries that a page adds without a user gesture, so a site can't trap visitors. The app used to add its guard entry on page load and re-add it inside the Back handler. Neither counts as a gesture, so a real swipe or Back press went straight past the guard and left the website. Scripted `history.back()` doesn't apply that skipping, which is why the earlier checks passed. Now the app adds entries only while you're tapping, clicking or typing: each interaction tops up a cushion of 3 Back presses, and each Back uses one.

Verification:
- `npm test` (91 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build` and `npm run test:api` pass.
- In a fresh browser tab with another page in its history before the app, I used real clicks and recorded every history entry the app added: all of them were added during a user gesture.
- After clicking Explore Events, three Backs in a row stayed on Explore Events.
- Event details: Back closed them, then the next Backs were absorbed.
- Forum: community → post, then Back, Back, Back closed the post, then the community, then was absorbed.
- Forward changed nothing.

Limitations:
- **No protection before the first interaction.** A Back or swipe before you tap, click or type anything leaves the site, because browsers ignore entries added without a gesture.
- **At most 3 Backs absorbed.** A fourth Back in a row without touching the page leaves.
